speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me understand the cause, how many days have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: That clinical picture of a viral prodrome followed by a facial rash sparing the nasolabial folds is highly suggestive of Rubella (German Measles), but I need to confirm if the rash has spread to the palms and soles and if you've noticed any joint pain. Additionally, have you or your household been in contact with anyone diagnosed with a recent rash?
